name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
description: The decline barbell bench press is performed on a bench declined at 15–30 degrees, shifting emphasis to the sternal (lower) head of the pectoralis major. The decline position also reduces the range of motion and allows some lifters to handle more load than the flat bench press.

execution.starting_position: Set the bench to a 15–30 degree decline. Hook your feet under the foot pad. Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip. The bar should be over your lower chest when unracked.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure feet in the ankle pads before lying back. Position body so the bar aligns with the lower pectoral region when at chest level.
steps: Unrack the bar and hold it directly over the lower chest with arms extended.
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest, maintaining retracted shoulder blades.
Touch the lower chest lightly and press back up along the same arc.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Extreme decline angles (beyond 30 degrees) reduce pectoral stretch
Lowering the bar too high on the chest negates the decline-specific benefit
safety_considerations: Blood can rush to the head in the decline position — avoid very heavy singles if susceptible to this
Always use a spotter or safety catches
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower bar to lower chest. Press to full extension. ROM will be shorter than flat or incline due to bench angle.
coaching_cues: Press the bar in a straight line — the decline angle handles the arc naturally
Keep your lower back in contact with the bench at all times
